import functools

@functools.lru_cache(None)
def solve(board):
    # Sort board to reduce state space
    board = tuple(sorted(board))
    
    # Termination conditions
    # (1) one of the numbers is larger than the sum of all other numbers
    total_sum = sum(board)
    for x in board:
        if x > total_sum - x:
            return len(board)
            
    # (2) there are only zeros on the blackboard
    if all(x == 0 for x in board):
        return len(board)
    
    # Player A's turn to choose x, y
    # Player A wants to maximize the result
    max_cookies = -1
    
    # Try all pairs (x, y) for A to choose
    # We only need to try distinct pairs of indices
    possible_moves_a = []
    for i in range(len(board)):
        for j in range(i + 1, len(board)):
            possible_moves_a.append((i, j))
            
    for i, j in possible_moves_a:
        # Player B's turn to choose x+y or |x-y|
        # Player B wants to minimize the result
        x, y = board[i], board[j]
        
        # Option 1: B chooses x + y
        board_plus = list(board)
        board_plus.pop(max(i, j))
        board_plus.pop(min(i, j))
        board_plus.append(x + y)
        res_plus = solve(tuple(board_plus))
        
        # Option 2: B chooses |x - y|
        board_minus = list(board)
        board_minus.pop(max(i, j))
        board_minus.pop(min(i, j))
        board_minus.append(abs(x - y))
        res_minus = solve(tuple(board_minus))
        
        # B will choose the minimum of these two
        cookies_for_this_pair = min(res_plus, res_minus)
        
        if cookies_for_this_pair > max_cookies:
            max_cookies = cookies_for_this_pair
            
    return max_cookies

for n in range(1, 11):
    print(f"n={n}: {solve(tuple([1]*n))}")
